note: Replay goldens of std-lolo-kotlin (std-lolo-source with the Kotlin vocabulary): the cases of lolo-python.replay.goldens.json, each with its paired control, plus code-points. Each case feeds the lowered program (orb lower, field orb) as the program/read answer (program/read has no substrate host in goldens, G-STD-262), with the installed operator names seeded in the entity. The text is Kotlin in package generated, beside the Android shell's generated models (Entities.kt and Events.kt from orb compile -s android), so it imports nothing; the four course examples and the fixtures that orb compile accepts compile against them and the course examples give the kernel's answers (minus-unary and no-machine are rejected by orb compile of the installed 19.0.0, so their text is not compiled). Every operator that is not listed in the atom's operators, unary, infix or lambdaOperators is a warning and a throwing stub; the object/*, json/*, bit/* and the other families the Python atom also leaves out are among them, and so are the str/ and validate/ predicates that need a runtime type test.

cases.note: array/range with one argument is [0,n); with two it is [a,n). The one-argument form must not leave a placeholder.
array/range with one argument is [0,n); with two it is [a,n). The one-argument form must not leave a placeholder.
(- a b) is a subtraction; the unary template must not win over infix.
(- a) is a negation. The fixture does not pass orb validate (the checker rejects a unary minus), the lowered program is what the reader answers.
array/nth answers null past the end: a helper, with the default applied once.
Control of nth-past-end: the same read with no default.
object/get on a missing key answers null: a helper.
(/ a b) answers null when b is 0; default evaluates its argument once.
Control of divide-default: no default around the division.
A let inside a let body in expression position: one lambda per binding, because bindings are sequential.
A list whose head is a string that is not an operator is a list literal.
Control of list-plain: the head names an operator in the installed table, so it is a call.
An operator with no template is a named warning and a stub that raises when run, never a call to an undefined name.

cases.note: A string literal that looks like a template placeholder ({{0}}, {{type}}) reaches the output verbatim, quotes, backslash, newline and non-ASCII are escaped, and a map literal with a key that is not an identifier keeps the key quoted. Control: list-call (an ordinary string).

A dollar in a string is a template in Kotlin, so stringEscapes writes it as backslash dollar: the string cost $5 ${x} followed by a backslash and a dollar stays the same text when run. Control: string-literal, a string with no dollar.
String length, slicing, reversal, padding and splitting count code points, so an emoji is one character: the same answers as orb evaluate on "héllo😀x".
